cf.title: HashAggregate loses worker spill stats on rescan

input.subject: HashAggregate loses worker spill stats on rescan

verdict_reasoning: The only surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is a fixable scoping question at level 2 and does not stop review. The problem is stated with a reproducer, the fix copies how non-parallel HashAggregate counters behave across rescans, and the cost falls only on EXPLAIN ANALYZE of rescanned parallel plans. A committer who knows executor instrumentation should confirm the merge rule and the stable-branch target.

brief.title: Accumulate HashAggregate parallel worker stats across Gather rescans
brief.problem: When a Gather or Gather Merge is rescanned, EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows HashAggregate memory, disk and batch stats for parallel workers from the last execution only. A worker that spilled in an earlier scan shows one batch and no disk usage. This affects users who read EXPLAIN ANALYZE output; query results are correct.
brief.proposed_design: ExecEndAgg() stops overwriting the shared per-worker instrumentation slot and combines with what earlier workers stored there. Memory and disk usage keep the maximum across executions, and spill batches add up. The initial in-memory batch counts once, to match non-parallel HashAggregate across rescans.
user_visible_surface: EXPLAIN ANALYZE per-worker HashAggregate output (Memory Usage, Disk Usage, Batches) changes for rescanned Gather and Gather Merge.
author_claims: ExecEndAgg() overwrites the shared worker slot, so only the last execution is reported.
The bug dates back to commit 9bdb300dedf.
Query results are unaffected; this is a reporting bug only.
hash_batches_used is always at least 1 for hashed and mixed aggregates when ExecEndAgg() records it.
ExecAggInitializeDSM() zeroes the slot, but a Gather rescan does not, so replacement workers add to the existing count.
brief.thread_state: Osama Abdul Qader asked whether the batch-count assumption holds and whether any rescan could count the initial batch twice; Ayush answered both. Osama said he would reproduce and check test coverage, but no review result is visible yet.
unclear: The patch touches only nodeAgg.c and adds no regression test for parallel HashAggregate rescans.
The proposal does not say whether other nodes with shared worker instrumentation, such as Sort, Memoize or Hash, have the same overwrite problem.
The material does not say which stable branches the fix targets.
The proposal does not say how the reported values relate to the per-loop averages EXPLAIN shows elsewhere.

prior_attempts.what_is_different: P6 changed how generic parallel worker instrumentation accumulates across Gather rescans. This patch changes only the HashAggregate-specific shared stats slot in ExecEndAgg().

objections.title: Rescan semantics fixed for HashAggregate only, other worker-instrumented nodes left unchanged
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a plan where Gather is rescanned and the workers run both a HashAggregate and a Sort or Memoize. The HashAggregate worker lines would then cover all executions, while the sibling node's worker lines may still cover only the last one. The user compares the two and reaches wrong conclusions about which node spilled.
objections.argument: The patch touches only nodeAgg.c. The proposal does not say whether Sort, Memoize, Hash or IncrementalSort also write per-worker slots that a Gather rescan reuses. If they do, one EXPLAIN output would mix two meanings for worker stats, and with a stable-branch target that mix would ship in minor releases. Matching the non-parallel HashAggregate counters is a sound rule, but a committer would likely ask that it apply to every node with shared worker instrumentation, or that the proposal say why only HashAggregate needs it.
objections.author_must_show: Do Sort, Memoize, Hash and IncrementalSort lose per-worker stats on Gather rescan, and if so, why fix only HashAggregate?

critic.reasoning: The patch touches only nodeAgg.c, and the thread does not say whether Sort or Memoize overwrite their worker slots in the same way. Hash already keeps maxima across rescans, so per-node fixes have precedent and the request stays a scoping question.

refuted.title: Fix covers HashAggregate only, other worker-instrumented nodes left unexamined
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a rescanned Gather that has both a HashAggregate and a Sort, Hash or Memoize below it. After the patch, the HashAggregate worker lines combine all executions, while the other nodes may still show only the last one. The user compares the lines without knowing they mean different things.
refuted.argument: The patch touches only nodeAgg.c. The proposal does not say whether the other nodes that copy stats into a per-worker shared slot at shutdown follow the same pattern. If they do, each node needs its own merge rule, and a new node with shared instrumentation has nothing that reminds its author to add one. A committer would likely want this checked before backpatching to stable, so that back branches do not get a one-node change that later fixes for other nodes then have to match.
refuted.author_must_show: Do Sort, Hash, Memoize and other nodes with per-worker shared instrumentation lose stats on Gather rescan in the same way, and if so, will they share one merge rule?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The added point that new nodes have no reminder to add a merge rule applies to all shared worker instrumentation, which this patch does not introduce.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable branches, and the fix changes EXPLAIN ANALYZE worker output in minor releases.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: ExecEndAgg() gets a HashAggregate-specific merge rule for the shared worker slot that later changes must keep correct.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Do Sort, Memoize, Hash and IncrementalSort lose per-worker stats on a Gather rescan, and if so, why does the patch fix only HashAggregate?
Which stable branches does the fix target, and is changed EXPLAIN ANALYZE worker output acceptable in a minor release?
Can the reproducer from message #1 become a regression test with stable output for parallel HashAggregate rescans?
How should a reader relate the combined memory, disk and batch values to the per-loop averages that EXPLAIN shows for the same node?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows parallel executor instrumentation and the HashAggregate spill code. No committer has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for changed EXPLAIN ANALYZE worker output on every back branch that gets the fix, and for the merge rule staying correct when the HashAggregate counters change.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered both review questions within a day in message #3.

priority.reason: The patch is a 1.8 KB change to nodeAgg.c that fixes wrong EXPLAIN ANALYZE output for rescanned Gather over HashAggregate. Only users who read such plans benefit, and the remaining point is a scoping question.

provisional_note: Without the code, the review could not check that the initial batch counts once in every rescan and worker-reuse case. It also could not check that the patch changes no shared struct, which matters for back branches.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Summary Sort workers Stats in EXPLAIN ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes EXPLAIN ANALYZE so that Sort node statistics from parallel workers are summarized (average and peak sort space used, sort method, number of workers) instead of being printed per worker. This follows the approach already used by show_incremental_sort_group_info() and is meant to reduce output size when many workers are used.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After a review pointing out issues (summary only in non-VERBOSE mode, reporting workers planned rather than launched, unclear text format), the author posted a revised patch, but the patch later failed regression tests on all platforms. A reviewer asked for an updated patch, none was posted, and the entry was marked Returned with Feedback for lack of an update.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This has been marked as RwF based on the lack of an update.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow setting parallel_workers on partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow the parallel_workers reloption on partitioned tables, so that the planner uses it to choose the number of workers for a Parallel Append over the partitions. A later version also let grouping relations take the setting from the partitioned table they read, for partitionwise aggregation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley questioned the semantics: a high setting on the partitioned table can request more workers than the partitions use, and the number does not shrink when the planner or run-time pruning removes partitions. Laurenz Albe and Amit Langote agreed the design needed more thought, and Amit Langote suggested a separate parallel_append_workers option. The thread then stalled, the patch stopped applying, and Daniel Gustafsson marked it Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If someone sets the partitioned table's parallel_workers high so that
they get a large number of workers when no partitions are pruned
during planning, do they really want the same number of workers in
queries where a large number of partitions are pruned?

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallelize correlated subqueries that execute within each worker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build parallel plans for queries with correlated subplans when each subplan runs entirely within one parallel worker, so no Param value has to pass between workers. After review, the design changed to treat PARAM_EXEC params as parallel safe by default, track required params on each rel, and insert a Gather node only where that set is empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread shows no author reply after Tomas Vondra's July 2024 review, and the entry was returned with feedback in October 2024. That review found that regression tests failed on a changed plan in select_parallel, reported a compiler warning, and listed code comments. It also said no reviewer was able to confirm that the PARAM handling is correct.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And in general the patch looks reasonably simple and clean, but my knowledge of PARAM intricacies is pretty much nil, so I'm hesitant to claim the patch is correct.

precedents_retrieved.title: speeding up GIN build with parallel workers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch splits a GIN index build between parallel workers, each scanning a range of heap blocks and building its own rbtree of entries. The workers send sorted entries through shared memory to the leader, which merges them and writes each key once; the leader later also takes part as a worker.
precedents_retrieved.objection: In April Robert Haas moved it to the next CommitFest because it had too little review and too few comments. He also found no parallel-safety check for expression indexes, workers opening the heap and index with no lock, and no agreement on the gin_shared_mem GUCs. Michael Paquier returned it with feedback mainly because of Heikki Linnakangas's suggestion to keep the rbtree but flush it to tapes and merge them with the tuplesort.c machinery from Peter Geoghegan's parallel B-tree patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we flushed the tree to a tape instead, then we could perhaps use the machinery that Peter's parallel B-tree patch is adding to tuplesort.c, to merge the tapes.

precedents_retrieved.title: explain to report bucket and memory stats for TupleHashTable nodes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds bucket counts and peak memory statistics to explain analyze output for nodes that use a TupleHashTable, such as HashAggregate, HashSetOp and Bitmap Heap Scan. It also splits memory accounting into separate contexts for the hashtable and the tuples.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The hash spill to disk commit (1f39bce02) already added most of the instrumentation, and the author asked whether the patch still served a purpose. Jeff Davis said the extra detail should go under VERBOSE or a new explain option. The patch then stayed Waiting on Author from March, and Daniel Gustafsson closed the entry when no new activity followed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This thread has stalled and the patch has been Waiting on Author since March,
and skimming the thread there seems to be questions raised over the value
proposition.

precedents_retrieved.title: improve DEBUG1 logging of parallel workers for CREATE INDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the DEBUG1 message for parallel CREATE INDEX to report parallel workers launched as well as planned. It later grew into a CREATE INDEX (VERBOSE) option, with matching REINDEX (VERBOSE) output, that reports parallel worker use at INFO level.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it after Michael Paquier pointed to Tom's view that such details should come from an extended EXPLAIN rather than VERBOSE options on more commands. Michael also asked how clients would consume the output. The author wrote that the best approach needs more discussion, and that fixing only the REINDEX DEBUG1 output did not make much sense.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm +-0 about the
VERBOSE option attached to more commands, as it is a bit harder for
clients to catch the information wanted.

precedents_retrieved.title: system load consideration hook for parallel workers
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Tom Lane, Peter Geoghegan
precedents_retrieved.summary: Before starting parallel workers, check the current system load and reduce the number of workers when the system is busy, so parallel query does not slow down other sessions at peak load. The author proposed a hook for this and later posted a POC patch that measures CPU load and picks the worker count from the free CPUs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that a load-based control for parallel workers alone is premature before there is field experience with parallel query, and that the problem covers all process types. He also did not trust system load metrics as a gatekeeper, since load averages lag by about a minute, and found the POC code platform-specific and poorly documented. He suggested refining the existing process-count settings instead, and closed the entry as not favored by the community.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We don't yet have enough field experience with the parallel query
facilities to know what kind of use patterns there are and what systems
for load management we need.  So I think building a highly specific
system like this seems premature.

precedents_retrieved.title: logicalrep_worker_launch - counting/checking the type limits
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes logicalrep_worker_launch() so it checks only the worker limit for the type being launched: the tablesync limit for tablesync workers and the parallel apply limit for parallel apply workers. It also applies the same garbage-collection retry to parallel apply workers that tablesync workers already get, and fixes a copied comment in logicalrep_sync_worker_count().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after a long period without activity. Amit Kapila asked whether the garbage-collection condition could be reproduced and whether a crashed leader worker would restart the server anyway, and the author never answered. The entry moved to Waiting on Author, and the author withdrew it when the commitfest manager asked him to answer or withdraw.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Did you try to reproduce this condition, if not, can you please try it
once? I wonder if the leader worker crashed, won't it lead to a
restart of the server?

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't shut down Gather[Merge] early under Limit.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Don't shut down Gather[Merge] early under Limit.
Reverted commit(s): Fix buffer usage stats for parallel nodes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert part of commit 19df1702f5.

Early shutdown was added by that commit so that we could collect
statistics from workers, but unfortunately, it interacted badly with
rescans.  The problem is that we ended up destroying the parallel context
which is required for rescans.  This leads to rescans of a Limit node over
a Gather node to produce unpredictable results as it tries to access
destroyed parallel context.  By reverting the early shutdown code, we
might lose statistics in some cases of Limit over Gather [Merge], but that
will require further study to fix.

roaster_notes.note: P6 is the only close relative. Its recorded reason says the earlier fix was not the best one but does not say why, so it gives no failure scenario that applies here. P12 is about Gather shutting down early under Limit and destroying the parallel context, which this patch does not do. The thread does not point to any earlier discussion of the same idea.

The only user-facing change is EXPLAIN ANALYZE output, and the patch copies how non-parallel HashAggregate counters already behave across rescans. Neither precedent's recorded reason applies: P6 gives no specific reason, and P12 is about early shutdown destroying the parallel context.

The proposal has no persistent or cross-node state: it changes how ExecEndAgg() fills a transient shared-memory instrumentation slot used only for EXPLAIN ANALYZE, with no on-disk, WAL, catalog, protocol or struct change. Only nodeAgg.c is touched, so a stable-branch backpatch should not raise ABI concerns, though this cannot be confirmed without the code.

The patch changes only how EXPLAIN ANALYZE combines HashAggregate memory, disk and batch stats from parallel workers across Gather rescans. Only the user who runs the query can see these stats, and the patch adds no new privilege, data exposure, escalation path or unbounded resource use, so there is no security angle to object to.

From the maintenance angle this is a small, contained bugfix. ExecEndAgg runs once per worker, so the patch adds no per-tuple, per-query or per-backend cost, and its semantics follow how non-parallel HashAggregate counters already behave across rescans. The one concern above is about consistency with other nodes, not about the fix itself.

This is a bug fix to EXPLAIN ANALYZE reporting inside nodeAgg.c. No existing feature, setting or extension can correct per-worker HashAggregate stats that ExecEndAgg() overwrites on a Gather rescan, so this angle finds no alternative. [P6] and [P12] concern other instrumentation fixes, and their recorded reasons do not apply here.

This is a bugfix to EXPLAIN ANALYZE output that is wrong today for any rescanned Gather or Gather Merge over HashAggregate. A one-file change has no cost for non-users, and Postgres does not require demand evidence to fix wrong output. The design questions, such as how to combine values across rescans and whether Sort, Memoize and Hash have the same overwrite problem, belong to other angles.
